contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #146: Positive metric entropy for the standard map.

Actual standard sine-map orbits q_(i+1)=2q_i+k sin(2 pi q_i)-q_(i-1) modulo one; K=2 pi k>0, M=K+4. Fix a central q_e and vary theta=q_(e-1) using real lifts on each finite path. Selected indices j_plus,j_minus>=2 are unbounded.

definitions.good: At a selected index j, tau_j-tau_l>=c(j-l) for every 1<=l<j, tau_(j+1)-tau_j>=c, and upsilon_j-upsilon_(j+1)>=c, upsilon_(j+1)-upsilon_(j+2)>=c; tau_l=log_M max(|t_l|,|t_(l-1)|), upsilon_l=log_M max(|u_l|,|u_(l-1)|); t_0=0,t_1=1; u_0=1.
definitions.common_solution: Both outward solutions satisfy u_1_minus+u_1_plus=v(q_e), where v=2+K cos(2 pi q).
definitions.success: At theta_star+h/L the same two indices are good for some common normalized solution, allowed to depend on h, with no endpoint smallness or rematching imposed; L=max(|t_j_plus(theta_star)|,|t_j_minus(theta_star)|), h in [-1,1].

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 146 (Positive metric entropy for the standard map.; papers: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/146.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

For the exact standard sine map f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k sin(2 pi x),y+k sin(2 pi x)) modulo Z^2 and normalized Lebesgue area m, there exists k_0>0 such that h_m(f_k)>0 for every k>=k_0 (main:entropy). Downstream claim, not established by this mission.

There exist delta,gamma>0 and C,M_0 finite such that for every M>=M_0, i integer, n>=1, the event min(log_M||T_(i,i-n)||,log_M||T_(i,i+n)||)>=(1-delta)n and log_M||T_(i-n,i+n)||<=delta n has probability <=C exp(-gamma n) (can:theorem); unverified downstream.

A configuration satisfying can:small-solution has at least c_1 n increasing pairs of good indices with |tau_j_plus-tau_j_minus|<=3/5, for fixed small delta and large n (can:many-good, can:matching); not established here.

For fixed observation bounds and h>0, the weighted product estimate E[1_fast W 1_(H>h)]<=C(E W+M^(-sigma n)) P(H>h/2) holds for all sufficiently large M and arbitrary sufficiently long bridges with log_M||T_(a,b)||>=c_b(b-a) (bridge:theorem); unverified downstream.
For all sufficiently large parameters and all integers n>=1, e_n<=e_(2n)<=C e_n+C/n, where e_n=E[1-log_M||T_(0,n)||/n] (scale:doubling); unverified downstream.

Under a sequence of zero-exponent parameters, scale:selection and scale:limits give the stated dyadic normalization, locally finite nonnegative measures off affine arrays, stationarity, four-point property, and terminal integrability; unverified downstream.
The limit measures satisfy shape:exclusions and the nonaffine slow, one-exterior-ray, or two-exterior-ray classification of shape:classification; unverified downstream.

The capped-deficit balance end:balance has positive terminal value H_Phi; the terminal contribution is strictly less than H_Phi and the invariant remainder is nonpositive, giving end:contradiction; unverified downstream.

With c=99/100 and base matching |log_M L_plus-log_M L_minus|<=3/5, for every eta>0 there exist eta_prime>0 and M_eta such that for every M>=M_eta, every fixed central coordinate, every base coordinate and every pair j_plus,j_minus>=2 good at the base for a common normalized solution, the real eta_prime-neighborhood of its success set has Lebesgue measure <=eta. All constants are independent of the selected indices. This is the literal assertion can:local-scarcity.

For every fixed 2/3<c<1 and alpha>=0 with 2 alpha<3c-1, the complete uniform scarcity statement of C_LOCAL_SCARCITY holds with goodness defined using this c and base matching discrepancy at most alpha. All orbits are those of the exact sine map; constants depend only on c,alpha,eta, not on coordinates, base solution, or unbounded selected indices.

At any base good index j, with L_j=|t_j(0)|, xi=L_j(theta-theta_star), B_l=M^(-c(j-l)), the rescaled displacements and first derivatives are O(B_l), and |D^p q_l|<=C_p B_l^p M^(1-pc) for 2<=p<=9. The quotient E=t_(j-1)/t_j has |D^p E|<=C_p M^(-c) for 0<=p<=8. Constants are uniform in j.

For 2/3<=c<1, an eighth-order inverse chain with 1<=s<=8, p_i>=1, sum p_i=8 and d_i>=1 has exponent H=-1+d_1+d_s+sum(min(d_i,d_(i+1))-c max(d_i,d_(i+1)))-c sum(p_i d_i) at most 8-15c-(1/8)sum(d_i-1). Consequently L_j^2|D^8 R_j|<=C M^(8-15c), uniformly for every finite selected j.

For the actual rescaled sine paths with nonzero limiting slopes, a positive-measure Hausdorff limit of success sets is impossible, including opposite limiting cosines after normalization by max(the quadratic phase-discrepancy coefficients,1/K).

For the actual rescaled sine paths whose second normalized slope r tends to zero, every possible slow-denominator scaling gives an affine reciprocal, fast secant, or eighth-order remainder incompatible with a degree-at-most-seven polynomial identity on positive measure.

Hausdorff compactness of success-set closures, interpolation at eight distinct limiting successful points away from finitely many poles, and the real analytic identity principle convert a positive-measure limit into the forbidden identities. Absence of such limits implies a uniform positive neighborhood width for each eta>0.

The four declarations in LocalScarcity certify: (i) for every eight real depths >=1 and every real c>=2/3 the expanded inverse-chain exponent is at most 8-15c-(sum(depths)-8)/8; (ii) the four alternating quadratic equations at 0,1,2,3 have only the zero solution; (iii) c>2/3 and 2 alpha<3c-1 make the three stated error exponents negative; and (iv) no real polynomial of natural degree at most seven equals X^8. No sine dynamics, measure estimate, or full scarcity theorem is encoded.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

namespace LocalScarcity

def total8 (x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7

def minEdges (x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  min x0 x1 + min x1 x2 + min x2 x3 + min x3 x4 +
    min x4 x5 + min x5 x6 + min x6 x7

def maxEdges (x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  max x0 x1 + max x1 x2 + max x2 x3 + max x3 x4 +
    max x4 x5 + max x5 x6 + max x6 x7

theorem eighth_chain_exponent
    (x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 c : ℝ)
    (h0 : 1 ≤ x0) (h1 : 1 ≤ x1) (h2 : 1 ≤ x2) (h3 : 1 ≤ x3)
    (h4 : 1 ≤ x4) (h5 : 1 ≤ x5) (h6 : 1 ≤ x6) (h7 : 1 ≤ x7)
    (hc : (2 : ℝ) / 3 ≤ c) :
    -1 + x0 + x7 + minEdges x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
      - c * maxEdges x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
      - c * total8 x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
      ≤ 8 - 15 * c - (total8 x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 - 8) / 8 := by
  let A := minEdges x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
  let V := maxEdges x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
  let T := total8 x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7
  have e0 : 8 * min x0 x1 ≤ x0 + 7 * x1 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x0 x1, min_le_right x0 x1]
  have e1 : 8 * min x1 x2 ≤ 2 * x1 + 6 * x2 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x1 x2, min_le_right x1 x2]
  have e2 : 8 * min x2 x3 ≤ 3 * x2 + 5 * x3 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x2 x3, min_le_right x2 x3]
  have e3 : 8 * min x3 x4 ≤ 4 * x3 + 4 * x4 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x3 x4, min_le_right x3 x4]
  have e4 : 8 * min x4 x5 ≤ 5 * x4 + 3 * x5 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x4 x5, min_le_right x4 x5]
  have e5 : 8 * min x5 x6 ≤ 6 * x5 + 2 * x6 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x5 x6, min_le_right x5 x6]
  have e6 : 8 * min x6 x7 ≤ 7 * x6 + x7 := by
    linarith [min_le_left x6 x7, min_le_right x6 x7]
  have hmin : 8 * A ≤ x0 + x7 + 9 * (x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6) := by
    dsimp [A, minEdges]
    linarith
  have htotal : T = x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 := rfl
  have hidentity : A + V = 2 * T - x0 - x7 := by
    dsimp [A, V, T, minEdges, maxEdges, total8]
    linarith [min_add_max x0 x1, min_add_max x1 x2, min_add_max x2 x3,
      min_add_max x3 x4, min_add_max x4 x5, min_add_max x5 x6,
      min_add_max x6 x7]
  have hsum : 8 ≤ T := by
    linarith
  have hmax : 7 ≤ V := by
    dsimp [V, maxEdges]
    linarith [le_max_left x0 x1, le_max_left x1 x2, le_max_left x2 x3,
      le_max_left x3 x4, le_max_left x4 x5, le_max_left x5 x6,
      le_max_left x6 x7]
  have hcritical : x0 + x7 + A - ((2 : ℝ) / 3) * (V + T) ≤ -T / 8 := by
    linarith
  have hproduct : 0 ≤ (c - (2 : ℝ) / 3) * (V + T - 15) :=
    mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hc) (by linarith)
  change -1 + x0 + x7 + A - c * V - c * T ≤ 8 - 15 * c - (T - 8) / 8
  nlinarith

theorem alternating_quadratic
    (a b c d : ℝ)
    (h0 : c + d = 0)
    (h1 : a + b + c - d = 0)
    (h2 : 4 * a + 2 * b + c + d = 0)
    (h3 : 9 * a + 3 * b + c - d = 0) :
    a = 0 ∧ b = 0 ∧ c = 0 ∧ d = 0 := by
  constructor
  · linarith
  constructor
  · linarith
  constructor <;> linarith

theorem uniform_error_margins
    (c alpha : ℝ) (hc : (2 : ℝ) / 3 < c) (ha : 2 * alpha < 3 * c - 1) :
    10 - 15 * c < 0 ∧ 2 - 3 * c < 0 ∧ 1 - 3 * c + 2 * alpha < 0 := by
  constructor
  · linarith
  constructor <;> linarith

theorem degree_seven_cannot_be_eighth_power
    (P : Polynomial ℝ) (hP : P.natDegree ≤ 7) :
    P ≠ Polynomial.X ^ 8 := by
  intro h
  subst P
  norm_num at hP

end LocalScarcity

claims.natural_statement: For every fixed 2/3<=c<1 and actual sine path with a base good selected index j, set L_j=|t_j(0)|, xi=L_j(theta-theta_star), B_l=M^(-c(j-l)). For all sufficiently large M, all |xi|<=1, and all 0<=l<=j, the displacements and first derivatives are O(B_l), and |D^p q_l|<=C_p B_l^p M^(1-pc) for 2<=p<=9. The quotient E=t_(j-1)/t_j is defined throughout this interval and has |D^p E|<=C_p M^(-c) for 0<=p<=8. Constants and the parameter threshold depend only on c and derivative order, not on j or the orbit.

Fix 2/3<c<1 and alpha>=0 with 2 alpha<3c-1. For actual sine-path configurations with the base goodness, common solution, and matching hypotheses of C_SCARCITY_EXT, any sequence M->infinity whose second normalized selected slope r tends to r_0>0 has no positive-measure Hausdorff limit of success-set closures. This includes opposite limiting cosines, normalized by max(the quadratic phase-discrepancy coefficients,1/K).

Fix 2/3<c<1 and alpha>=0 with 2 alpha<3c-1. For actual sine-path configurations with the base goodness, common solution, and matching hypotheses of C_SCARCITY_EXT, any sequence M->infinity with second normalized selected slope r->0 has no positive-measure Hausdorff limit of success-set closures. The affine reciprocal, fast-secant, and eighth-order slow-remainder cases exhaust the denominator regimes.

For a sequence of success-set closures with a positive-measure Hausdorff limit, a degree-at-most-seven polynomial relation with errors uniformly tending to zero and right sides converging locally uniformly away from finitely many limiting poles admits coefficientwise polynomial extraction at eight distinct limiting successful points. When clearing the limiting analytic denominators yields a real analytic function on R, the resulting equality is an identity. If every nonempty Hausdorff limit along M->infinity has measure zero, then for every eta>0 a positive neighborhood width and sufficiently-large-M threshold work uniformly over the configurations.
